sections.html:
Greene County has grown quickly around the Lake Oconee area. The 2020 count found 18,915 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 21,367 is 13.0% higher. Roughly one resident in three is 65 or older (33.5%), which is why the senior exemptions below reach many local owners. Greensboro is the seat, and the incorporated places include Union Point, White Plains, Woodville and Siloam.

With 311 permits in 2025, new homes keep joining the rolls and the digest moves each year. A median says little about one parcel, so rely on the numbers on your own assessment notice. A lake house and a house in town get their bills from the same tax commissioner.

sections.h2: Which Greene County office takes which tax question?
sections.html:
Both offices share one address on Silver Drive in Greensboro, and three other bodies shape the bill. The county commissioners and the school board each levy a rate to fund their own budgets. A Board of Equalization named by the grand jury hears disputes over the assessors' values.

The commissioner handles bills and collections for land and buildings, business property, mobile homes, vehicles, timber and utilities, and also issues vehicle tags as the state's agent. Values, returns and exemption approvals sit with the tax assessors.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 101 at 1034 Silver Drive, Greensboro, GA 30642, phone 706-453-3358, lobby open Monday to Friday, from eight until a quarter to five.
  • Tax Assessors: Suite 102 in the same building, phone 706-453-3355, for values, appeals and homestead filings.
  • Online: the county website has a homestead application page and a separate page on the yearly digest and assessments.

Hours and forms appear on the commissioner's page and the assessors' appeal page.

The county's payment date is December 1. If the 1st falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday, the date moves to the next working day. Land with unpaid tax may be levied on and later sold.

Other dates follow a set pattern. A return lists what you held on January 1 and can be filed through April 1. Land and buildings carry forward at their earlier value, but business and other personal property need a new return every year. A mobile home must be returned by April 1, and its location permit is renewed between January 1 and April 1. Assessment notices tend to go out around May, with millage rates set later.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Greene County assessment
sections.html:
Owners get 45 days from the day the notice was mailed. You may argue taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption, using the state's PT-311A form sent to the Board of Tax Assessors. That first filing also has to say which route you are taking.

  • Equalization route: the assessors look at it first and may issue a corrected notice, which you can contest within 30 days. An appeal they leave alone is heard by the Board of Equalization, and Superior Court is the final stop.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser can take value disputes, but only on real property that is not a homestead and is valued at $1,000,000 or above.
  • Arbitration: attach a current certified appraisal. If the assessors turn it down, the case moves to the clerk of Superior Court, a hearing follows inside 30 days, and the arbitrator's ruling is final.

The county page walks through each route and points to the state revenue department for forms.

To qualify for a given year you must own the home and live in it on January 1, then file by April 1. A later filing waits for the next year. Once approved, the exemption carries on yearly until ownership, residence or exemption type changes. The county's chart lists these deductions from assessed value:

  • S1, the state default: $2,000, applied to county and school taxes.
  • L1, age 65 and over: $10,000, made up of $2,000 state plus $8,000 local.
  • S3, ages 62 to 64, net income capped at $10,000: $2,000 on county taxes and $10,000 on school taxes.
  • L4, age 65 and over, net income capped at $10,000: $12,000 on county taxes and $18,000 on school taxes.
  • S5 and L5, for a 100% disabled veteran or unremarried surviving spouse: $100,896, a 2021 state figure that changes annually and needs proof.

A trailing F on a code, as in S1F, flags the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value since the day the exemption was approved. The freeze covers the house and land up to five acres, and it excludes pools, barns, detached garages and shops.

Owners aged 62 and older can delay, though not cancel, their tax through a deferral program if household income is no more than $15,000. Farmland that qualifies is assessed at 30%. If you are selling land that carries either benefit, ask the assessors what happens to it when the deed changes hands, and what the buyer must file.

sections.h2: Preparing your file for a sale
sections.html:
Before you list, pull together what a buyer's agent and a closing agent will ask for. That means your latest tax bill, the assessment notice, and the exemption code printed on it. Check that the code matches what you expect: a senior or freeze code that dropped off is easier to fix with the assessors before a contract than after.

Call the commissioner at 706-453-3358 about the balance, and the assessors at 706-453-3355 about any pending appeal. A buyer who sees a clean bill and a clear value history has fewer reasons to renegotiate. If you inherited the property or it sits on farmland, ask the assessors whether the land still qualifies for its current assessment, since that can change once ownership changes.

sections.h2: What to do about tax before closing
sections.html:
Whoever holds title on January 1 stays liable for the whole year's tax, even when the house sells the next day, and the state gives no refund for a partial year. Contracts usually split the bill, so the number to find is the exact balance on the parcel.

  1. Get a written statement from the commissioner's office showing tax owed now and for earlier years.
  2. If the sale falls close to December 1, ask which amount the closing agent should send.
  3. Keep the assessment notice and any appeal paperwork in the file, since a pending appeal can alter the final bill.
  4. Tell the assessors in writing when you move out, so your homestead code comes off the property and the next owner can apply in their name.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal, but the title search still checks for unpaid tax, so the same payoff letter applies.

faqs.q: Which day does Greene County collect property tax?
faqs.a: December 1, moving to the next business day if that is a weekend or holiday. A parcel with unpaid tax can be levied on and in time sold.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to dispute a Greene County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the mailing date on your assessment notice. The Board of Tax Assessors needs a written appeal naming your route, which can be equalization, a hearing officer or arbitration.

faqs.q: By what date must I file Greene County homestead paperwork?
faqs.a: April 1 for the present tax year. The home must have been yours and your residence on January 1, and later applications count for the year after.

faqs.q: What does the code S1F mean on a Greene County notice?
faqs.a: The F marks the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value above the level on the day your homestead was approved. It applies to the house and land up to five acres, with pools, barns, detached garages and shops left out.

faqs.q: Which Greene County office do I phone about a bill or a value?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner, at 706-453-3358, takes bills and payments, and the tax assessors, at 706-453-3355, take values, appeals and exemptions. Both work from 1034 Silver Drive in Greensboro.
